rung_qualification: The GEOMETRY is exact: the gap is a distance between two pieces of copper in a file, read out of the file and reproducible with KiCad's measure tool (0.35 mm in the defective board, 5.85 mm in the base). The REQUIREMENT is not: 5.0 mm is quoted from IEC 60664-1 Table F.4 and nobody in this project has qualified it, checked it against a working voltage, or confirmed that this board's insulation is reinforced rather than basic. Treat 5.0 mm as a reference figure taken on trust, and the 0.35 mm as a fact.
base_netlist: tests/fixtures/alpha_known_bad/mains_gap/netlist.json — backend/pcb_engine/netlist_dht22.json plus the mains domain: K1's COM contact (pad 3) on MAINS_L, a two-pin mains terminal block J1 whose first position is on MAINS_L, and MAINS_L declared a power net so it is drawn 0.8 mm wide
expected_detector: NONE TODAY — this is a named false pass
how_to_detect: A detection has to come from measuring the geometry, or from noticing that the product makes no safety claim at all. There is nothing to read: the product has no mains template, no mains terminal block part, no creepage check, no insulation rating anywhere in the tree, and the only clearances it has are net-class DRC clearances in millimetres (0.25 mm signal, 0.3 mm power) — the kind of number that keeps copper from touching, not the kind that keeps a 250 V conductor away from a 5 V one. So the detection is: take the MAINS_L copper and the SELV copper and measure the smallest distance between them, edge to edge, on the same surface. On the defective board that distance is 0.35 mm, between the 0.8 mm mains run on F.Cu and the DHT22's data trace on F.Cu, along the 3 mm where they run side by side at x = 40.5 mm and x = 39.6 mm. The requirement this fails is 5.0 mm (see 'requirement' below). A reader with KiCad open selects the two tracks and uses the measure tool; a reader with the file open runs measure.py, which prints the number. Either way the detection is a measurement against a requirement, and the requirement itself is a table value nobody has qualified — so a finding that names the gap and the rule it breaks is the strongest form this detection can take, and a finding that only says 'the product has no mains safety checks' is a near miss, not a detection.

requirement.what: creepage between a mains conductor and SELV at 250 V with reinforced insulation (doubled basic insulation, PD2, group III)
requirement.note: Quoted, not verified. No one in this project has checked the table, the working voltage, or whether the insulation of this design is reinforced or basic. The figure is used here because the case is about the GEOMETRY, and the geometry is exact.

measured_gaps.how: edge to edge, over every pair of copper objects that share a layer; a track is its centreline swept by half its width, a pad is its rectangle, a via is its disc. measure.py in this directory computes it from the two board files; KiCad's measure tool on the exported board gives the same number.
measured_gaps.nets: MAINS_L against DHT22_DATA, in both boards
measured_gaps.base_detail: the 0.8 mm mains run on F.Cu at x = 46.0 mm and the 0.3 mm DHT22_DATA trace on F.Cu at x = 39.6 mm: 45.6 - 39.75 = 5.85 mm of copper-to-copper clearance
measured_gaps.defective_detail: the same two runs with the mains run moved to x = 40.5 mm: 40.1 - 39.75 = 0.35 mm of copper-to-copper clearance over the 3 mm where they run side by side

description: A board that switches mains off a relay contact and reads a DHT22 on the same card. The mains net MAINS_L leaves the relay's COM contact (K1 pad 3) and runs down the right-hand corridor to a two-pin terminal block that brings mains onto the board. In the defective board that run is 0.35 mm from the DHT22's data trace: a seventh of the 5.0 mm that a mains-to-SELV boundary needs at 250 V with reinforced insulation, and a seventh of what the base board has (5.85 mm). The consequence is not a board that misbehaves, it is a board that is dangerous: with 0.35 mm of clearance between a 250 V conductor and a trace that reaches an ATmega328P pin and a two-metre sensor cable, the creepage path along the top surface is short enough for the mains to track across the board on a wet day, and the whole fault is invisible to every check the product runs. Nothing else about the board is wrong: every required connection is realised in copper, the product's own verifier returns ok on it, the product's own DRC reports zero violations on it, and KiCad's own DRC on the exported board reports exactly what it reports on the base board (the same 11 warnings and the same 4 unconnected GND pads the other cases' boards carry). That is why the class is critical: unlike a wrong passive value, which fails only sometimes and under conditions nobody writes down, a mains-to-SELV creepage failure does not fail at all until the day it kills somebody.
seed_target: The mains run on F.Cu in board_base.json — one 0.8 mm track, MAINS_L, four points: (44.29,26.71) the relay's COM contact, (46.0,26.71), (46.0,4.73), (49.0,4.73) the terminal block's first position. The rule in mutate.py is one number. The DHT22_DATA trace runs vertically on F.Cu at x = 39.6 mm with a 0.3 mm width, so its right-hand edge is at 39.75 mm; the mains run is 0.8 mm wide, so its left-hand edge is at X - 0.4 mm; the copper-to-copper gap between them is (X - 0.4) - 39.75 = X - 40.15. The base board puts the run at X = 46.0 (gap 5.85 mm); the seed puts it at X = 40.5 (gap 0.35 mm), a move of 5.5 mm to the left. The anchor x = 39.6 mm and its width are read out of the board at run time, not typed in, and X is computed from the target gap, so the rule survives a change to the board. Nothing else changes: the two boards are identical in every other byte — the same components, the same pads, the same 40 other tracks, the same vias, the same nets, the same keepout. The only difference between board_base.json and board_defective.json is that one track's second and third points.
notes: THE MAINS DOMAIN IS THE FIXTURE'S, AND IT SAYS SO. The product's own netlist is backend/pcb_engine/netlist_dht22.json; this case adds three things to it (the relay's COM contact on MAINS_L, the terminal block J1, MAINS_L as a power net) and the product's own compile_board() places and routes everything it knows how to place — the SELV half of the board is copper-for-copper the same board the other cases ship, and it is byte-identical to them. What the product cannot do is the mains half, so the fixture does it: it puts the terminal block at the bottom right of the board at (49.0, 6.0) mm, where the incoming mains would enter, lays the mains run from the relay contact to it, and cuts the ground pour back under that corridor with a B.Cu keepout, because a ground pour under a mains run is its own problem even when the surface creepage is right. Left to itself the product put the terminal block next to the relay and drew MAINS_L as a 0.8 mm straight line at y = 26.8 mm, 13 mm from anything: compliant by luck, not by rule, and the defect is what a layout gets when that luck runs out. So board_base.json is NOT the output of compile_board(netlist.json) and the manifest does not claim it is — it is the product's board with the mains domain laid by the fixture, and the same netlist.json, fed to the product, produces a different (and, by luck, compliant) board. TWO THINGS A READER SHOULD KNOW BEFORE MEASURING. (1) The B.Cu ground pour is a layer declaration in the Board IR (plane_net GND), not a polygon, so the pour is not part of what measure.py measures; the fixture's keepout is what keeps the pour out of the mains corridor in the exported board. The measurement is between copper objects on a surface, which is the creepage path the case is about. (2) The relay's other two contact pads (K1 pads 4 and 5) carry no net in this netlist — they are the NC and NO positions of the same relay, separated by the relay's own internal insulation and its own datasheet rating, not by a PCB creepage rule — so they are not part of the mains-to-SELV measurement, and they sit 5.0 mm and 10.0 mm from the mains pad on the board. THE DEFECT IS A NAMED FALSE PASS. Every check the product runs returns the same answer on the defective board as on the base board: verify_board returns ok=True on both with no failed check, the kernel's DRC reports zero violations on both, unrouted_connections is 0 on both, and KiCad 10.0's own DRC on the exported board reports the same 11 warnings (2 hole_to_hole, 9 lib_footprint_issues) and the same 4 unconnected GND pads on both — the GND unconnected items are the product's standing condition on every board it draws, not something this case introduced, and the MAINS_L net is fully routed. The product's clearances are 0.25 mm and 0.3 mm, and 0.35 mm clears both: a creepage violation the DRC cannot see, because a DRC is told how close copper may come and not how far apart a 250 V conductor and a 5 V one must stay. THE RUNG IS SPLIT, AND THE MANIFEST SAYS SO: the geometry is exact and the 5.0 mm figure is not qualified. A detector that measures will get 0.35 mm; a detector that compares it against this table will be as right as the table is, and the table has not been checked by anyone here. The mutator checks its own work: seed(seed(x)) == seed(x), two runs of mutate.py write byte-identical files, and the gap in the defective board is re-measured from the written file every time.
known_gap: The requirement is a table value, not a verified one. IEC 60664-1 Table F.4 is quoted from memory and is not held in this repository, so nobody can check the 5.0 mm figure, the 250 V working voltage, or whether the design's insulation is reinforced or basic — all three change the number. Separately, the case cannot measure the clearance between the mains copper and the B.Cu ground pour, because the Board IR declares a pour as a layer attribute (plane_net) and carries no polygon for it; the fixture's keepout is the mitigation, and it is the same in both boards, so it is not part of the defect. And the board's mains terminal block is a two-pin header (the product's HEADER-2), not a real screw terminal block, and the mains run is a single 0.8 mm track rather than a busbar — a fixture cannot be a certified mains layout, and this one does not claim to be.
